commits.message: HeadingLevel's comment sits on it and names setext headings; MdToken keeps its own (rich-unfiled-791c.n0a3)
Heading level is typed 1-6 at the parser, every level's own key and the rule's are pinned, and the docs name them (rich-unfiled-791c.n0a3)

Markdown draws headings, rules and link URLs in Rich 15's styles, each heading level from its own key (rich-unfiled-791c.n0a3)

markdown.h2-h4, hr and link_url now match rich.default_styles in Rich 15,
and h5/h6 exist. headingStyle read markdown.h${min(level, 4)}, so a theme
setting h5 or h6 did nothing; it now reads markdown.h${level}, as Rich's
Heading reads markdown.{tag}. A test pins h1-h6, the rule and both link
URL forms against Rich 15's rendered segments.

Keys Rich defines that this renderer never reads (h7, paragraph, text,
emph, code_block, list, h1.border) are not added. markdown.kbd is a real
gap in behaviour, filed as rich-unfiled-791c.k2zi.

TextInput measures the width it draws, the cursor's cell at the end included (rich-unfiled-791c.dn30) (#462)

* TextInput measures the width it draws, the cursor's cell at the end included, and keeps that cell in view when the value overflows (rich-unfiled-791c.dn30)

The single-line field sizes its content as its text plus, past the text's
end, the cell the cursor stands on. measure() left that cell out, so a field
laid out at its measured width hid its cursor whenever the cursor sat at the
end, and the viewport's scroll clamp did the same to any value wider than
the field: typing at the end of a long value showed no cursor. Both now read
one derivation, singleLineExtent.

A multi-line value measured as if it drew brackets and a placeholder; it
draws neither, so its maximum is its widest line shown plus its cursor's
cell.

* TextInput's viewport starts at a glyph boundary, so a wide glyph never pushes the cursor out of view, and multi-line measure leaves a scroll arrow its cell (rich-unfiled-791c.dn30)
